枝.meaning: A lumberjack's daughter won't let him cut down the old <part>tree</part>, so she climbs up, ties a hammock to its lowest <part>branch</part> and moves in with a kettle and a cat. He gives up. Now the family has a guest room on a <kanji>bough</kanji>.
枝.on: She props an old knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld against the trunk as her front door.
枝.kun: Every morning she fries an <sound>e</sound>gg for her pet <sound>du</sound>ck, up on the branch.

君.meaning: A parrot works the front desk of a grand hotel. It grips a <part>baton</part> in one claw to tap the bell, then opens its <part>mouth</part> and greets every guest the same way: 'Good evening, sir!' The dog, the toddler, the duchess: to the parrot, everyone is <kanji>mister</kanji>.
君.on: One guest arrives wrapped up in a silk co<sound>coon</sound>, and the parrot bows anyway.
君.kun: It hands each guest a room <sound>key</sound> and sends a <sound>mee</sound>rkat bellhop to carry the bags.

康.meaning: A janitor finally retires to a garden <part>shed</part>. He leans his old <part>mop</part> in the corner, puts his feet up and has nothing to clean but his teacup. After a month the bored mop sprouts daisies. He has found his <kanji>ease</kanji>.
康.on: Each afternoon he sits in the doorway licking an ice cream <sound>cone</sound>, very slowly.

洞.meaning: Twin fox cubs, the <part>same</part> down to the last whisker, dig a hideout behind a waterfall, where a curtain of <part>water drops</part> hides the way in. Their mum can never tell which one sneaked out at night. It's the perfect <kanji>den</kanji>.
洞.on: They line the floor with big lumps of bread <sound>dough</sound> for pillows, warm and squishy.
洞.kun: A bat lodging in the roof shares his <sound>ho</sound>tdog and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men with them.

暇.meaning: On her day off, a firefighter climbs a <part>rope ladder</part> to her roof and lies in the <part>sun</part> with a lemonade, ignoring the phone ringing below. The cat climbs up to join her. Nothing to do but nap: pure <kanji>spare time</kanji>.
暇.on: From the roof she dangles a line into the pond and teases a big orange <sound>car</sound>p.
暇.kun: She lets one bare <sound>hee</sound>l hang over the edge, and a <sound>ma</sound>ma pigeon perches on it.

衝.meaning: At a <part>crossroads</part> on a farm, two snails race from opposite lanes, each dragging a <part>heavy</part> shell piled high with luggage. Neither will slow down or step aside. Three days later, with a tiny click, they <kanji>collide</kanji>.
衝.on: A crowd of beetles bought tickets to watch the slow-motion <sound>show</sound>.
衝.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' hisses the slower snail, and jabs the other with a <sound>coo</sound>k's wooden spoon: to thrust.

潮.meaning: Every <part>morning</part> a crab sets up a deckchair at the very edge of the sand. By noon the <part>water drops</part> lap at its claws, then its knees, so it drags the chair back a few steps, grumbling. The crab never wins against the <kanji>tide</kanji>.
潮.on: As the sea rises, a wave snatches the crab's pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker and carries it away.
潮.kun: '<sound>She</sound> took my pearls! <sound>Oh</sound>!' wails the crab, shaking a claw at the sea.

岐.meaning: Halfway up a <part>mountain</part>, a hiker reaches a spot where the trail splits like a <part>branch</part>: left to a waterfall, right to a café. She flips a pancake to decide, and it lands on her head. Every good hike has a place where the path must <kanji>branch off</kanji>.
岐.on: On the signpost at the fork hangs a brass <sound>key</sound>, labelled 'For whichever way you pick.'

虐.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> crowns himself boss of the toy box. He makes the teddy bears line up by height, locks the crayons in a <part>drawer</part> and roars at any doll caught smiling. The toys whisper about a revolt. He loves to <kanji>tyrannize</kanji>.
虐.on: At night the toys slip a le<sound>ggy</sound>, <sound>yu</sound>cky rubber spider into the tiger's <sound>coo</sound>kie jar.
虐.kun: He even orders a toy <sound>shee</sound>p to fetch him a <sound>ta</sound>co every hour.

誇.meaning: At the pet show, a goldfish hires a <part>showman</part> to give a <part>speech</part> about him: 'He swam round this bowl ten thousand times! He once scared a cat!' The goldfish puffs up so much he floats to the top. He does love to <kanji>boast</kanji>.
誇.on: In the next cage, a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala yawns through the whole speech.
誇.kun: A parrot in the crowd heckles: '<sound>Ho</sound>, <sound>co</sound>ld fish, sit down!'

驚.meaning: A carousel <part>horse</part> stuck on its pole for fifty years is finally set free. It trots out of the fairground and freezes in <part>awe</part> at its first real meadow, its first cow, its first puddle. Every single thing is a <kanji>wonder</kanji>.
驚.on: A lost tourist holds up her map. '<sound>Kyo</sound>to?' she asks, stretching out the start, and the horse gapes at the map too.
驚.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter, a <sound>do</sound>lphin and a <sound>ro</sound>bin rush over to meet the amazed horse and bring it a <sound>coo</sound>kie.

敏.meaning: A pickpocket at the market reaches for an old lady's purse, but <part>every</part> time his hand gets close she snaps open her <part>fan</part> and swats his knuckles, without looking up from the melons. He gives up and slinks away. That's quick-witted <kanji>cleverness</kanji>.
敏.on: Still not looking up, she sweeps the melon rind he tripped on into a rubbish <sound>bin</sound>.
敏.kun: She keeps her coins in her <sound>sa</sound>ri, a <sound>to</sound>ffee tin and a jar with an <sound>ee</sound>l in it.

鋭.meaning: An <part>imp</part> with nothing to do sharpens a <part>gold</part> pencil all day: fine enough to pop bubbles across the room, then fine enough to split a raindrop in two. By evening the tip is too <kanji>pointed</kanji> to write with.
鋭.on: So he uses it to carve a tiny smiling face on an <sound>a</sound>corn.
鋭.kun: Then he spears <sound>su</sound>shi off a <sound>roo</sound>k's plate and a sardine off a <sound>do</sound>lphin's.

脂.meaning: A chef opens a diner on the <part>moon</part> and fries everything in bacon drippings. The astronauts all call it <part>delicious</part>, but each one floats home a little rounder, and the plates glisten for weeks. The secret ingredient is <kanji>fat</kanji>.
脂.on: The chef scrubs the greasy pans with an old knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
脂.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs an astronaut, licking grease off a cook<sound>boo</sound>k full of <sound>ra</sound>men recipes.

掲.meaning: A shipwrecked sailor jams his <part>anchor</part> upright in the sand and lashes a striped <part>sunshade</part> to its top, then waves the whole thing until a passing plane spots it. When you're lost, the smart thing is to <kanji>put up</kanji> something bright.
掲.on: The pilot drops him a birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke on a little parachute.
掲.kun: 'Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm,' he tells a <sound>ca</sound>rp in a rock pool, and holds the sunshade higher.

坂.meaning: A grumpy mole is <part>anti</part> anything flat. All night he shovels <part>soil</part> under one end of the bowling green until the whole lawn tilts, and the bowls roll off into the pond. By morning the green is a <kanji>slope</kanji>.
坂.on: The bowlers sit at the bottom eating toast and <sound>hon</sound>ey while the bowls dry.
坂.kun: A lady in a <sound>sa</sound>ri sleds down it on a <sound>ca</sound>rdboard tray.

雇.meaning: A baker hires a <part>sparrow</part> to work the shop <part>door</part>: it pecks the handle to open it, chirps hello to every customer and takes payment in crumbs. Sales double. It's the best bird she ever chose to <kanji>employ</kanji>.
雇.on: On weekends she also takes on a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala to guard the cream buns.
雇.kun: She pays the sparrow in <sound>ya</sound>rn, which it knits into socks for its <sound>toe</sound>s.

棚.meaning: An owl who collects things nails a plank between two limbs of her <part>tree</part> and lines it with treasures: buttons, a teaspoon, a snow globe with <part>twin moons</part> inside. Every night she dusts it with a wing. Every owl needs a <kanji>shelf</kanji>.
棚.on: Once a week the farmer below rinses it with his garden <sound>hose</sound>, and she hoots at him.
棚.kun: Her newest treasure is a <sound>ta</sound>co wrapped in <sound>na</sound>an.

駄.meaning: A <part>plump</part> pony refuses to walk to the fair, so the farmer ends up carrying the <part>horse</part> on his back, puffing up the hill with hooves dangling round his ears. The pony munches an apple the whole way. What a <kanji>burdensome</kanji> pet.
駄.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck hops onto the pony's head, adding to the load.

墓.meaning: At <part>sunset</part>, a retired robot digs a hole in the <part>soil</part> for his worn-out vacuum cleaner, plants a daisy on top and plays it a soft beep. It cleaned for forty years. It deserves a proper <kanji>grave</kanji>.
墓.on: Beside it he plants a tiny <sound>bo</sound>nsai tree to keep it company.
墓.kun: Then he plays a slow tune on a little <sound>ha</sound>rp, standing <sound>ca</sound>lm in the dusk.

項.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> writes its memoirs at a tiny <part>workbench</part> beside the bath, one squeaky line at a time. Every time the water ripples, it starts a fresh section about bubbles. The whole book is one-line chapters, each a new <kanji>paragraph</kanji>.
項.on: Between sections it nibbles the tip of an ice cream <sound>cone</sound>.
項.kun: It balances <sound>u</sound>don, <sound>na</sound>an and a toy <sound>jee</sound>p on the nape of its neck.

是.meaning: A fussy giant polishes his <part>giant boot</part> until it shines like the <part>sun</part>, sets it toes-first by the door, nudges it a hair to the left, then back. Only then does he smile. Everything must be <kanji>just so</kanji>.
是.on: He sprinkles lemon <sound>ze</sound>st on his porridge, exactly three flakes.
是.kun: On the doormat he sets a toy <sound>ko</sound>ala with a <sound>re</sound>d bow, and points at it: this one.

随.meaning: A <part>flag bearer</part> marches down a <part>ramp</part> onto a ferry, and behind her come forty ducklings, a goat and a man who just likes flags. Nobody knows where the ferry is going. They just <kanji>follow</kanji>.
随.on: The ducklings chase a rolling yu<sound>zu</sound> fruit, and an <sound>ee</sound>l slithers after them.
随.kun: Their <sound>ma</sound>ma waddles behind, then a goat with a sore <sound>knee</sound>, then a <sound>ma</sound>rching band.

邦.meaning: After years at sea, a sailor leaps off his boat, ties his <part>pennant</part> to the nearest <part>corn stalk</part> and hugs it. The farmer is baffled. But to the sailor, every row of corn means one thing: his <kanji>home country</kanji>.
邦.on: The farmer welcomes him with a blast from his garden <sound>hose</sound>.
邦.kun: His mum hands him a <sound>coo</sound>kie, and he drops to one <sound>knee</sound> to eat it.

揮.meaning: A little old fisherman sees an <part>army</part> of seagulls swooping for his chips. He heaves his <part>anchor</part> over his head and swings it round like a lasso, roaring. The gulls turn back. Never doubt what a man will <kanji>brandish</kanji> for his chips.
揮.on: Then he waves his house <sound>key</sound> at them too, for good measure.
揮.kun: He shakes his <sound>foo</sound>t at a <sound>roo</sound>k that's still eyeing his fish.

惨.meaning: A snowman pays a <part>visit</part> to his cousin in the desert. By lunchtime he is a puddle with a carrot in it and a scarf on top, his <part>heartbeat</part> a tiny drip. He looks utterly <kanji>wretched</kanji>.
惨.on: His cousin, a cactus, offers him an ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae to cool down.
惨.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat in a <sound>jee</sound>p tries to scoop him up with a <sound>me</sound>lon rind.

哀.meaning: A peacock loses every feather in a storm and turns up at the ball in a borrowed <part>garment</part>: a soggy tea towel. He opens his <part>mouth</part> to announce himself, and only a squeak comes out. Everyone pats his head. He looks <kanji>pathetic</kanji>.
哀.on: He tries to hide in a corner behind some <sound>i</sound>vy.
哀.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs a duchess. '<sound>Wah</sound>,' sobs the peacock, into her <sound>re</sound>d hanky.

肩.meaning: Locked out under the full <part>moon</part>, a sleepy giant tries the handle, sighs, then leans into the <part>door</part> with one big bump, and it pops open. The cat inside barely yawns. Some jobs need the <kanji>shoulder</kanji>.
肩.on: His dog lifts its head out of its <sound>ken</sound>nel and wags.
肩.kun: He rubs his sore arm, <sound>ca</sound>lm again, and eats a cold <sound>ta</sound>co.

珍.meaning: A <part>king</part> holds a contest for the oddest pet. A <part>person</part> from the hills brings a goldfish with long curly <part>whiskers</part> that hums when you stroke them. The king trades his crown for it on the spot. Such a fish is <kanji>rare</kanji>.
珍.on: The fish strokes its whiskers like a wise old man stroking his <sound>chin</sound>.
珍.kun: In the palace it eats nothing but <sound>me</sound>lon, yu<sound>zu</sound> and <sound>ra</sound>men.

獣.meaning: In the <part>rice field</part> at night, a <part>dog</part> spots a <part>sparkle</part> of eyes and a huge <part>mouth</part> full of teeth. He barks bravely, then sees it's only a scarecrow with a kettle on its head and a moth on its nose. Still, he tells everyone he chased off a wild <kanji>animal</kanji>.
獣.on: The farmer gives him a shiny <sound>jew</sound>el collar as a medal.
獣.kun: The <sound>ke</sound>ttle clanks, the <sound>mo</sound>th flutters off, and the dog is <sound>no</sound>t so brave after all.
